messages:
arjun: Quick question — ran a short throughput/latency sweep for the new 30B q4f16 build across us-west and eu-west. Numbers look pretty different at p95. Link to charts: https://redwood.internal/bench/1987 (chart images embedded)

sara: can you paste the key numbers? quick skim of charts is blocked on my laptop rn

arjun: sure — p50/p95 tokens/s for request pattern A (avg len 120):
- h100-us-west: 420 t/s p50, 28 ms p95 per token
- h100-eu-west: 410 t/s p50, 46 ms p95 per token
- a100-us-west (q4f16): 260 t/s p50, 85 ms p95 per token
- a100-eu-west (q4f16): 250 t/s p50, 140 ms p95 per token

mike: whoa eu-west A100 p95 is rough. is that kernel selection? or networking?

arjun: initial suspicion is kernel + region-specific machine packing. eu-west cluster we have mixed GPU tenancy and a slightly older kernel build (cuda/rocm variants). logs show some extra memcpy stalls.

janelle: is KV cache warmup accounted for? p95 can spike if cache miss on cold pop.

arjun: bench sim had warmup phase, we excluded first 30s. these p95s persist afterwards.

sara: did you try fused attention kernel vs default? any diff when forcing fused path?

arjun: yes — switching to fused-attn reduces eu-west A100 p95 from 140ms -> ~95ms, and us-west A100 p95 from 85ms -> 60ms. H100 still wins overall.

mike: ok so actionable items: 1) prefer fused-attn kernel on A100 pools, 2) recommend autoscale headroom change for eu-west. thoughts on numbers?

janelle: for Dedicated, we target a concurrency that keeps p95 token latency under 100ms for interactive SLAs. current per-GPU concurrency target for A100 we set to 12 for this model; with fused-attn maybe 14. H100 can do 20 safely.

arjun: i ran a quick capacity calc: peak qps target = 8000 tokens/s sustained. If we choose concurrency 14 on A100 (250 t/s p50 ~ so conservatively 200 effective t/s at p95), need ~40 A100 GPUs in eu-west to hit throughput with 25% autoscale buffer (for spikes). With H100 at concurrency 20 and 400 t/s effective, need ~20 H100 GPUs.

sara: sounds right. also factor in reserved burst lanes for canary + smoke tests — keep 2 GPUs per pool out of rotation.

mike: agree. we should also codify fallback routing: if eu-west A100 pool p95 > 120ms for 30s, route 30% of traffic to H100-us-west until eu metrics recover. avoid full failover.

janelle: please capture that as a policy:
```
fallback_policy:
  metric: token_latency_p95
  threshold_ms: 120
  window_s: 30
  fallback_route: h100-us-west
  fallback_fraction: 0.3
  cooldown_s: 300
```

arjun: added to the draft runbook at https://redwood.internal/runbooks/dedicated-provisioning#1987

infra-bot: deployment:kernel-update-a100-eu started by mike at 1987656000 — rolling to 10 nodes :rocket:

sara: mike — when that lands, can we rerun the same sweep with stress pattern B (many small prompts) + cold cache sim? need to see tail behavior.

mike: will do. ETA for kernel rollout ~2 hours. i'll kick off stress run once the nodes are upgraded.

janelle: longer term: investigate packing changes in eu-west to reduce cross-tenant memory pressure. add to Q2 infra backlog.

arjun: summary action items:
- mike: roll kernel -> run stress pattern B (logs + charts) and post results here
- janelle: add eu-west packing investigation to backlog (Q2)
- sara: update capacity calc doc with H100/A100 numbers and recommended GPU counts + 25% autoscale buffer + 2 reserved burst GPUs
- arjun: update runbook with fallback_policy and link to bench charts

mike: noted. i'll post results as a follow-up message. :thumbsup:

sara: thanks all — this feels like a safe initial sizing.

arjun: one more note — quantization q8 gave slightly higher throughput on A100 but degraded sample quality on the eval set (regression on rouge/em for a small prompt cohort). we'll keep q4f16 for now and mark q8 as experimental.

janelle: good call. we'll add an eval alert if quality drops >2% on critical prompts after any quantization change.

infra-bot: run:throughput-sweep-1987654321 completed, artifacts: https://redwood.internal/artifacts/bench-1987654321.zip
